scholarships.title: Royal Society - Research Ireland University Research Fellowship

existing.description: The Royal Society University Research Fellowship is an eight-year independent research fellowship for outstanding early career scientists, with a dedicated Royal Society - Research Ireland arm for fellowships hosted at a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body in the Republic of Ireland. Research Ireland meets the cost of awards based in the Republic of Ireland, while UK-based awards are funded by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade. Funding covers a contribution to salary, indirect and estate costs, equipment and research expenses, staff costs, and relocation and visa costs for the applicant and dependants. The 2027 round closed on 9 September 2026 with decisions due by 31 May 2027.
eligibility: Between three and eight years of research experience, excluding career breaks, since the award of a PhD by the closing date of the round
Research within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences, including biological research, biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics
Fellowship must be hosted within a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body for the Ireland arm
Must not already lead a research group or be named Principal Investigator on an external award
Must not hold a tenure-track faculty position or permanent academic post
Must not hold or have held a nationally competitive research fellowship equivalent to a URF (five or more years, portable, covering salary and research costs)
existing.eligibility_summary: For postdoctoral researchers with three to eight years of research experience since their PhD at the round's closing date, working within the natural sciences, who do not already lead a research group, hold a permanent or tenure-track post, or hold an equivalent nationally competitive fellowship. Applicants based in the Republic of Ireland must meet the additional eligibility set out in the Research Ireland scheme notes and host the fellowship within a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body.
benefits: Contribution to salary plus indirect and estate costs
Contribution to research assistance and other staff costs
Relocation and visa support for the applicant and dependants
Access to Royal Society career development and engagement opportunities
coverage: Contribution to the award holder's salary
Equipment costs and research expenses including consumables and travel
Contribution towards research assistance salary and associated indirect and estate costs
Contribution to staff costs including PDRA, PhD studentships and technical support
Relocation and visa costs for the applicant and dependants
requirements: Submit the host institution support letter to urf@royalsociety.org separately from, and prior to, the application; exceptional cases not flagged beforehand will not be considered
Meet the Research Ireland-specific eligibility requirements for Republic of Ireland applicants
Provide a research proposal and costs for eight years
documents: Research proposal and eight-year costed budget submitted through Flexi-Grant
Institutional host support letter from the Research Ireland Eligible Research Body, submitted to and flagged with the Grants team before the application itself
Evidence of research experience since PhD award
application_method: Prior submission of a host institution support letter to the Grants team
existing.selection_notes: Applications pass eligibility checks, are assessed by at least two members of the relevant Research Appointment Panel, then independent peer review, then interview. Irish and UK candidates are assessed together through the normal Royal Society peer review process. Historical success rates are 7% (2022/23), 6.4% (2023/24), 6.8% (2024/25) and 6.3% (2025/26). Shortlisted applicants are invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society.
existing.best_fit: Postdoctoral researchers in the natural and biomedical sciences, three to eight years post-PhD, seeking an eight-year independent research career at an eligible host institution in the Republic of Ireland or the UK.
existing.notes: The scheme does not support clinical or interventional research on humans at the individual or group level, nor social sciences or humanities. Applicants of any nationality may apply and those requiring a visa can use the Global Talent Visa fast-track endorsement. Holders of Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions postdoctoral training fellowships, and Royal Society Dorothy Hodgkin Fellows meeting the research experience requirements, may apply.
existing.duration: 8 years (years 6-8 subject to a mid-fellowship review at the start of year 4)
existing.application_period: Annual competitive round. The 2027 cycle ran from 14 July 2026 to 9 September 2026, with decisions by 31 May 2027.
existing.deadline_display: The 2027 round is listed as Status: Closed, with Open date 14 July 2026, Close date 09 September 2026 and Decision by 31 May 2027. No dates are published for the following round.
